newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: cricket-Morrison ready if NZ need him, says Blain.
newsitem.headline: cricket-Morrison ready if NZ need him, says Blain.

text.p: AUCKLAND, March 7 - Auckland cricket coach Tony Blain says experienced pace bowler Danny Morrison is ready if New Zealand need a replacement for Geoff Allott in the second test against Sri Lanka in Hamilton next week.
Left arm paceman Allott was ruled out of the first test starting today in Dunedin because of a back injury and is to go to Christchurch for a scan for a possible stress fracture.
Blain told NZPA today he read nothing sinister in the selectors not recalling Morrison or putting him on standby last night when they knew Allott was in doubt.
"I think a lot of that has to do with the pitch, and certainly from our game down there at Carisbrook before this test we didn't think the pitch really suited fast bowlers," Blain said.
"When we played there it turned out to be a good batting strip and the selectors may instead have been looking for a good stock bowler instead of an attacking bowler.
"I don't know what their thinking is, but I know they want Danny to be able to bowl at full pace if he is recalled."
Blain said Morrison, who was dropped after the first test against England at Eden Park, had shown marked improvement in his form.
"At the moment he is at about 90 percent of full fitness," Blain said.
"Danny is bowling short spells of extreme pace at the moment. It isn't quite consistent but it is just about there."
However, Blain said that meant little when the weight of his experience and his ability to lift himself for the big occasion was taken into account.
"Let's not forget that he didn't bowl too badly against England on a very flat deck where he also had problems with his footing," the former New Zealand wicketkeeper said.

"He has certainly improved a great deal on that form and when you consider his enormous experience, his desire to play for New Zealand again and the fact that he is on the verge of his best form then you have to consider him.
"If they (New Zealand selectors) need him for the second test then I'd have no problems in recommending him. Put it this way, he's in far better form than he was at Eden Park in the first test."
With New Zealand's stocks in the fast-medium seam bowling ranks looking ragged, Morrison could well be back before the end of the summer.
The other options for the selectors to consider are Otago's David Sewell and Northern Districts' Alex Tait, who has impressed at Shell Trophy level.
